passages.context: The archived message, read in full in the retrieved page. It carries the claim in the standard wording: the folded napkin had to do with the Master and Servant, every Jewish boy knew this tradition, the wadded napkin meant I'm done, and the folded napkin meant I'm coming back. Registered as the earliest independently archived instance located and therefore as a dated lower bound on the claim's circulation.
passages.notes: The scriptural text the message quotes at John 20:7 reads that the cloth was folded up and lying to the side, which is a modern version's wording and not that of the King James or Douay-Rheims translations from which the word napkin comes.

work.description: The earliest independently archived instance located of the folded-napkin chain email, carrying the claim in its standard wording. Registered as dated evidence of the medium and the date of circulation. The scriptural text quoted inside the email is from a modern copyrighted English version reading folded up, which is where the claim's key word comes from; that version is described in consuming publications rather than reproduced.
